Code example

Optimize model serving latency

intermediate coding

Implement dynamic batching for model inference that groups concurrent requests to maximize GPU utilization while respecting latency SLOs.

What to notice

  • Use a background thread that collects requests until batch is full OR timeout expires
  • Each caller blocks on an Event until their result is ready
  • Balance max_batch_size (throughput) with max_wait_ms (latency)

Expected outcome

Concurrent requests are batched together, each getting their individual result back

Reference solution 
import time
import threading
from typing import List, Any
from queue import Queue

class DynamicBatcher:
    def __init__(self, max_batch_size: int = 8, max_wait_ms: float = 50):
        self.max_batch_size = max_batch_size
        self.max_wait_ms = max_wait_ms
        self.queue = Queue()
        self.worker = threading.Thread(target=self._batch_loop, daemon=True)
        self.worker.start()

    def predict(self, input_data: Any) -> Any:
        result_event = threading.Event()
        result_holder = {}
        self.queue.put((input_data, result_event, result_holder))
        result_event.wait()
        return result_holder["result"]

    def _batch_loop(self):
        while True:
            batch = []
            first = self.queue.get()
            batch.append(first)
            deadline = time.time() + self.max_wait_ms / 1000
            while len(batch) < self.max_batch_size and time.time() < deadline:
                try:
                    item = self.queue.get(timeout=max(0, deadline - time.time()))
                    batch.append(item)
                except:
                    break
            inputs = [item[0] for item in batch]
            results = self._process_batch(inputs)
            for (_, event, holder), result in zip(batch, results):
                holder["result"] = result
                event.set()

    def _process_batch(self, batch: List) -> List:
        time.sleep(0.01)
        return [f"result_for_{item}" for item in batch]

Model serving architecture lab

Interactive diagram

Production model-serving stack

Rendering diagram…

Separate feature preparation, routing, and fallback handling so the serving path stays fast and resilient.

Worked example

Serve low-latency models inline with strict tail constraints

A checkout service needs fraud scores in under 60 ms p95 before approving a transaction.

Recommended choice

Deploy a lightweight online model behind a feature store cache with aggressive timeout and fallback behavior.

Why it fits

  • The request path cannot wait on heavyweight inference without harming checkout conversion.
  • Feature-store caching prevents redundant feature computation on the hot path.
  • Fallback rules keep the business moving if the model service degrades.

If you chose differently

Routing checkout traffic to a bulky model stack without timeouts turns every model incident into a customer-facing outage.

Interview-ready takeaway

The strongest answer includes explicit latency budgets, fallback actions, and how the score joins the transactional workflow.
